context: The integer n is positive. Recursion depth is the maximum number of calls that are active at the same time.
description: The left column, “Descend,” shows the chain recur(n) → recur(n−1) → … → recur(4) → recur(3) → recur(2) → recur(1). A brace spanning the column is labeled “Recursion depth n.” At the bottom, an arrow labeled “Reach the base case” points to the right column, “Unwind.” The sums on the right are faded to draw attention to the calls accumulating on the left.

frames.explanation: When execution reaches recur(1), all the outer calls are waiting for a child to return. There are n stack frames at once, including the top-level call. Only then does recur(1) return 1. Each outer call adds its own argument and releases its frame as it returns. The number of active calls at the deepest point gives a recursion depth of n and a stack space complexity of O(n).
frames.title: Recursion depth when summing

summary: The figure highlights how many calls accumulate before the recursive sum reaches its base case.
